title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: Zscaler
providers.scope_notes: Covers Zscaler (ZIA, ZPA, OneAPI via Authentication Service / ZIdentity). SaaS; OneAPI needs services linked to Authentication Service; legacy ZIA API needs an API subscription; Workflow Automation, Client Connector and ZDX API keys not covered.

controls.name: API client Status (enable/disable)
controls.what: A disabled client cannot get tokens, and its issued tokens are revoked.

controls.name: Delete API client
controls.what: Deleting a client revokes its tokens.

controls.name: Revoke access token
controls.what: Revoke a single active token by Client ID or JTI.

controls.name: Access Token Validity
controls.what: Sets token lifetime from 1 minute to 24 hours.
controls.setting: Add/Edit API Client > Access Token Validity

controls.name: API resources (scope)
controls.what: Client gets one API role per Zscaler service.

controls.name: API Client Access Policy
controls.what: Allow/Block rules by API resource and time window, one rule per client.
controls.setting: Administration > API > API Client Access Policy

controls_unknown: Source-IP restriction for OneAPI clients, ZPA keys or legacy ZIA sessions (Admin Sign-On Policy and ZIA restricted admin access pages do not state API coverage)
Whether the Authentication Service Admin Sign-On Policy or MFA applies to legacy ZIA API password logins
Whether deleting/disabling a ZPA API key or ZIA authorization server ends already-issued bearer tokens
Whether API client create/delete and token revoke appear as named actions in Authentication Service audit logs (documented actions are generic Create/Update/Delete)
Whether read-only (GET) API calls are recorded in any audit log
Expiry of JWT key pairs (zscaler-2) and Sandbox tokens
OneAPI rate limits (only legacy limits fetched)

authentication.summary: An API client in Authentication Service (ZIdentity) uses the OAuth 2.0 client credentials grant with a client ID and secret at <tenant>.zslogin.net/oauth2/v1/token (audience https://api.zscaler.com) and gets a JWT access token for OneAPI.

federation.details: Docs do not describe workload/OIDC federation for secret-based clients.

ip_restriction.boundary: API Client Access Policy criteria are time and API resources only; no source-IP criterion is documented. Whether the Admin Sign-On Policy applies to API clients is not stated.

lifetime.summary: Secret 30-365 days; access token 1 min-24 h

renewal.expiry_basis: Access token validity set per client (1 min-24 h); secret has its own 30-365 day validity
renewal.summary: Request a new token with the secret; rotate by adding a second secret (max two; a third replaces the most recent).

administration.summary: Admins with API Clients & Resources permission create, edit, enable/disable, delete clients and revoke tokens. Scope is one API resource (role) per Zscaler service.
administration.conditions: Zscaler services must be linked to Authentication Service; up to 256 API clients per tenant.

offboard.details: An API client represents an application or service, not a user.

inventory.details: API Clients page (Administration > API > API Clients) lists all clients and exports CSV; issued tokens on Administration > API > Tokens.

token_format.notes: JWT access token (bearer); client ID auto-generated.

log_sources.name: Authentication Service Issued Tokens page
log_sources.notes: Administration > API > Tokens; lists Client ID, JTI, issued/expires, status.

log_sources.name: Authentication Service audit logs
log_sources.notes: Data Explorer > Audit Logs > Authentication Service; Interface field shows API-based; stream to SIEM via NSS (auditlogtype ZID).

log_sources.name: ZIA audit logs
log_sources.notes: Data Explorer > Audit Logs > Internet & SaaS; records Admin UI and API actions; 6-month retention; NSS admin audit feed.

log_sources.name: ZPA audit logs
log_sources.notes: Records admin and API actions; Client ID column; 6-month retention.

credential_id_fields.notes: Generated for ZIA requests via OneAPI
API key client ID that made changes
Created by OneAPI; visible when Authentication Service enabled

lifecycle_events.notes: Generic Authentication Service audit action; client-specific category not listed

anomaly_cues: Tokens issued for a client outside its normal schedule (Issued At filter)
ZIA/ZPA changes with Interface API from unexpected Client IP
New secret added to an existing client

containment.steps: Disable or delete the API client (revokes its tokens), or revoke individual tokens on the Tokens page; remove secrets/keys.
containment.notes: Revoked tokens can no longer be used; disabling the client revokes its tokens.

unknown: Exact audit event name for API client and token actions
Whether token issuance is itself audited
Whether OneAPI GET calls are logged
